description: The identifier's own structure says the object is not the paper. Above admission (`replication-claim`, 700): a review object echoes its parent's title verbatim, so it fires replication arms on something that is not the study, and no amount of replication vocabulary in the text makes the identifier point at a paper. Two separately-labelled arms, kept as their own clauses so each can be audited and retired on its own evidence. (1) A `/reviews/` or `/decisions/` path segment is minted by the publisher for the review object (e.g. 10.7287/peerj.10325v0.1/reviews/2); such records echo the reviewed paper's title verbatim, so every replication phrase in the title fires on something that is not the paper. A narrowing worth doing later is anchoring the segment to known registrants rather than matching anywhere in the DOI. (2) A DOI ending in `.suppl` is the supplementary object minted alongside an article, not the article; terminal-anchored so it cannot fire on a DOI that merely contains the string. It is the identifier-side counterpart of the `supplementary-materials` work type in not-a-report-type, and the two overlap deliberately: different fields, either one alone is enough. Deposit-only registrants are a different kind of claim — a list of external facts about who mints what, not a pattern in the identifier — and live in their own spec, `deposit-registrant`.

measured.rationale: Arm 1 (/reviews/ | /decisions/), carried unchanged from the retired `non-article-doi` spec: a DOI path segment minted by the publisher for the review object itself, so the mapping is structural, not statistical.

Arm 2 (\.suppl$), new in the v2 rule book: a terminal ".suppl" is the identifier a publisher mints for the supplementary object of an article. Structural for the same reason as arm 1 — the claim is about what the registrant writes into the identifier, not about a rate estimated from a sample — and the terminal anchor is what keeps it that way: a DOI that merely contains the string is not claimed.
